aois.name: Bhopal Bhoj Wetland & Narmada Agro-Valley
aois.tagline: Coupled Hydro-Agricultural Subsidence & Canal Gradient Inversion

plainEnglishSummary.crisis: Heavy monsoon rainfall is trapped beneath dense tree and crop canopies behind the NH-46 road embankment, while intense tubewell pumping for wheat crops has collapsed the underground aquifer by -19.4 mm/yr, tilting the irrigation canal backward.
plainEnglishSummary.whyMissed: Normal optical satellites saw only a 92% white blanket of monsoon storm clouds, missing the pooled floodwater and underground soil sinking entirely.
plainEnglishSummary.howFound: DSpace's NASA-ISRO 24cm L-Band radar waves pierced through the clouds and tree canopy, catching water bouncing off tree trunks (+6.2 dB HH) and measuring millimeter ground subsidence with radar interferometry.
plainEnglishSummary.impactBefore: 14 villages flooded • 4,200 hectares of cropland ruined • ₹48 Cr potential loss
plainEnglishSummary.impactAfter: 14 villages drained • 4,200 hectares saved • ₹48 Cr economic loss prevented

mitigationPlan.actionDescription: Deploy pressurized 1,200mm siphon culverts beneath highway embankment and re-grade canal bed to 0.026% slope.

aois.name: Himalayan Wildfire-to-Landslide Slope Cascade
aois.tagline: Crown Ash Hydrophobicity & Monsoon Debris Runout

plainEnglishSummary.crisis: Intense pre-monsoon forest fires baked a water-repellent ash glaze across steep mountain slopes. Heavy monsoon rains cannot soak into the soil, saturating the bedrock shear plane and accelerating slope creep to 4.8 mm/day above the pilgrim highway.
plainEnglishSummary.whyMissed: Optical satellites only see black burnt trees, unable to measure sub-surface moisture or millimeter-scale slope sliding.
plainEnglishSummary.howFound: DSpace's dielectric microwave sounding measured extreme moisture trapped at the bedrock interface (ε = 41), while InSAR phase fringes revealed accelerating creep before catastrophic collapse.
plainEnglishSummary.impactBefore: Badrinath highway severance imminent • Factor of safety: 1.04 • 28,000 pilgrims trapped
plainEnglishSummary.impactAfter: Slope stabilized • Factor of safety raised to 1.62 • 28,000 pilgrims protected

mitigationPlan.actionDescription: Drill pressurized pre-stressed rock-bolts into stable phyllite toe and install debris-dissipation check dams.

aois.name: Coseismic Fault Slip & Gravity Canal Stress
aois.tagline: Kutch Mainland Fault Blind Thrust & Saline Water Upwelling
aois.hazardType: Coseismic Surface Rupture & Reverse Gradient Tilt

plainEnglishSummary.crisis: A magnitude 6.4 blind thrust earthquake along the Kutch fault lifted the northern canal block by 28.6 cm, snapping concrete liners and reversing the water flow backward into the main drinking water pump station.
plainEnglishSummary.whyMissed: Optical cameras cannot see invisible sub-centimeter land warping across flat desert landscapes or underground saltwater upwelling.
plainEnglishSummary.howFound: DSpace's L-Band interferogram mapped 2.4 concentric radar fringe circles (each circle = 11.9 cm offset) directly over the buried fault trace, isolating the cracked canal section in minutes.
plainEnglishSummary.impactBefore: Canal liner sheared • 340 structures flooded • Drinking water cut to 64,000 residents
plainEnglishSummary.impactAfter: Backflow wave arrested • Flexible siphon flume installed • Drinking water restored in 48h

aois.name: Samudra Tapu Glacier Melt & Surge (GLOF Risk)
aois.tagline: Basal Cryo-Lubrication & Moraine Dam Hydrostatic Breach
aois.hazardType: Glacial Lake Outburst Flood (GLOF) Imminent Trigger

plainEnglishSummary.crisis: Record summer heat melted 4.2 million m³ of glacier ice. Meltwater lubricated the glacier bedrock, triggering a 325 m/yr surge ramming directly into an unstable earthen dam holding back 12.4M m³ of water.
plainEnglishSummary.whyMissed: Mountain blizzards and high-altitude cloud cover hid the expanding meltwater lake and crevasse surge from optical view.
plainEnglishSummary.howFound: DSpace's GOFF pixel-offset radar tracked crevasse speed through blizzard conditions, detecting the 325 m/yr velocity spike and measuring 18 mm/wk dam crest bulging.
plainEnglishSummary.impactBefore: Catastrophic GLOF breach wave (42,500 m³/s) threatening Atal Tunnel and 18 villages
plainEnglishSummary.impactAfter: Lake level lowered by 8.5m via siphons • Controlled bedrock spillway opened • 100% GLOF averted
